author: reek
body: An act block used to take `synthetic-span` -- 0,0 -- because the CST `ActExpr` carries no token of its own. That put the one position-less node exactly where the most common effect error lands: `check-def` reports CDX2031 against `aexpr-span (def.body)`, and for any def whose body is an act block the diagnostic printed with no line:column at all. Most effectful code in the language has an act block for a body.

author: reek
body: The block now takes its first statement's span. On this chapter the CDX2031 reports at 48:5 -- the `print-line-uni` inside `needs-console` below -- where it used to report nowhere.

author: reek
body: The sidecar is `CDX2031@48:5`, not a bare `CDX2031`, and the difference is the whole point of this file. A bare code checks only that the error fired, and CDX2031 fired before the fix too -- it just fired with no line:column, because a 0,0 span prints no prefix at all. A code-only check therefore passes against the exact compiler this test exists to catch. The `@line:col` form is what can fail on a lost position, and `build/test.ps1` grew it for this.

author: reek
body: Run rather than assumed: against this compile's log, `CDX2031@48:5` matches, `CDX2031@10:5` does not, and bare `CDX2031` matches either way. The pin discriminates; the bare code does not.
